subject: Meditech MAP template + first draft (GDoc) — propose 30d eval + close timeline
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@meditech.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@meditech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Meditech MAP template + first draft (GDoc) — propose 30d eval + close timeline

Hi Ellen / Tom —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. As promised I’m attaching a short MAP template and a starter Google Doc with the initial scope pulled from our discovery notes. High level proposal: a 30-day evaluation focused on accuracy and latency at representative query volumes, with one-week checkpoints and a demo week to validate integrations and acceptance criteria. Target decision / procurement window: by 2027-04-25 so you can hit your Q2 rollout.

What I’ve attached/shared:
- MAP_Template_v1.docx (MAP scaffold — roles, success criteria, milestones)
- MAP_Week0_Sprint_Slate.gslides (week0 kickoff + roles slide)
- Starter GDoc (read/write link below) — I put owners next to each milestone so we have a clear RACI to start editing.

GDoc (starter): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-meditech-map-draft

Quick asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the primary technical contact for the evaluation (engineer name + email)?
2) Any baseline SLA/latency targets we should bake into the plan?
3) Are there any compliance constraints (data residency, SOC2 evidence) we need to capture on day 0?

If that looks good I’ll set the first check-in (week0 Kickoff) for 2027-03-21 and propose the demo week for 2027-04-05–04-09. If those dates don’t work we’ll adjust.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the doc together.

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Attachments: MAP_Template_v1.docx, MAP_Week0_Sprint_Slate.gslides
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@meditech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@meditech.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meditech MAP template + first draft (GDoc) — propose 30d eval + close timeline

Olga —

Thanks for the draft and the clear timeline. A couple quick clarifications before we start editing the doc: 

1) Data residency — for the pilot we need logs and any stored artifacts to remain in our AWS account (us-east-1). Is that supported for the trial?
2) Trial sizing — our initial workload for the pilot will be about 12k inference requests/day with peak bursts closer to 200 req/s. Is the MAP set up to validate both steady-state and burst performance?
3) Security evidence — can you include the most recent SOC 2 summary and a short note on audit logging retention? We’ll need that for procurement.

If you can confirm those items I’ll pull our engineer Tom into the GDoc and add functional acceptance criteria. The dates you proposed look reasonable; I’ll confirm after we validate internal availability.

Appreciate it —
Ellen
Director, Product Ops | Meditech Systems
ellen.park@meditech.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@meditech.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@meditech.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meditech MAP template + first draft (GDoc) — propose 30d eval + close timeline

Ellen — thanks for the quick review, and great questions. Short answers below and I updated the GDoc with a small "Security & Ops" section and an appendix for measurements. Link to the edited file is in the doc header. I also attached a customer-facing MAP we previously used as a reference (Meditech_MAP_v1.docx) 

1) Data residency: for the pilot we can run the inference in your AWS account using Redwood Private (VPC mode). That keeps all model execution and persisted logs inside your VPC; we only access metadata via the control plane if you opt in. I added a short footnote in the MAP and a step for a simple network runbook during week0.

2) Trial sizing: yes — the acceptance matrix now includes two performance lanes: steady-state (12k/day) and burst (200 req/s). We recommend running a synthetic traffic pattern during week2 test to validate autoscaling and latency SLOs. I added suggested load profiles and the scripts we typically use in the appendix.

3) Security evidence: attached is the SOC summary and an audit-log retention note in the doc. Procurement will still want the full artifacts; we can route those via an S3 share or an on-demand audit bundle.

Next steps I’ve updated in the MAP: 
- Week0 (2027-03-21): Kickoff + network runbook, stakeholder RACI review
- Week1 (2027-03-28): Integration + smoke tests at small scale
- Week2 (2027-04-04): Load test + acceptance validation (synthetic burst)
- Demo week (2027-04-05 to 2027-04-09): live demo + acceptance signoff window
- Decision window: target contract sign by 2027-04-25

If that works I’ll queue the calendar invites and add Tom as an editor to the GDoc.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: Meditech_MAP_v1.docx, SOC2_Summary.pdf
From: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@meditech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@meditech.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meditech MAP template + first draft (GDoc) — propose 30d eval + close timeline

Marissa / Olga —

This looks good to me. I’m happy to be the technical contact — tom.briggs@meditech.com. I’ll add the rest of our integration team to the GDoc this afternoon and confirm availability for the week0 kickoff (2027-03-21).

One note: for the week2 synthetic burst test we’ll need the exact load generator config so we can run it from our side in us-east-1. Marissa — can you drop the script and a short runbook into the appendix (or share a Drive folder)?

If all that’s in place, lock demo week 2027-04-05–04-09 on our calendar.

—Tom
Principal Engineer | Meditech Systems
tbriggs@meditech.com
